relation_statement: Every model-held parameter must carry the configured target floating-point dtype after the init-time cast, while remaining the same Parameter object the model references, under a sharded-init context.
observable_signal: param.dtype of each registered nn.Parameter compared against the configured target dtype at end of init
validity_precondition: parameters constructed inside a sharded-init (zero.Init) context, including tensors created with requires_grad=True
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO param dtype cast reassigns Parameter to a non-Parameter Tensor
evidence_from_fix: .to() returns a fresh non-Parameter Tensor; the model still held the original reference, so the model's Parameter kept the wrong dtype

relation_statement: All model parameters, including frozen (requires_grad=False) ones, must be bitwise restored after a checkpoint save/load round trip under sharded-optimizer training.
observable_signal: checksum of frozen parameters before save vs after load; presence of frozen parameter keys in the saved state
validity_precondition: model contains parameters with requires_grad=False; sharded parameter/optimizer state (ZeRO stage 3) enabled
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO3 checkpoint silently omits frozen (requires_grad=False) parameters from saved state
evidence_from_fix: checkpoint logic only iterated trainable parameters; frozen parameters were never written, so resume trains from random-initialised frozen weights

relation_statement: Each tensor-parallel rank's non-expert parameter shard must be saved and restored to the same rank after a checkpoint round trip when expert parallelism is enabled.
observable_signal: count of per-mp-rank model_states files vs tp_size at save; per-TP-rank parameter checksum before save vs after load
validity_precondition: MoE model with expert parallelism and tensor parallel size > 1 during checkpoint save/load
evidence_from_issue: MOE save_checkpoint with TP > 1 only writes mp_rank_00_model_states.pt — non-zero TP ranks lose non-MoE weights
evidence_from_fix: short-circuited with `if exp_dp_rank != 0: return` before saving per-mp-rank files; resuming silently loaded mp_rank_00 onto every TP rank

relation_statement: Each parameter's gradient must be routed into the reduction bucket belonging to that parameter's own group under multi-group sharded training.
observable_signal: group index bound in each backward hook vs the parameter's actual group id; per-group reduced-gradient mismatch when groups > 1
validity_precondition: sharded-gradient training (ZeRO stage 3) with more than one parameter group
evidence_from_issue: backward hook closure captures stale group index `i` — gradient routed to wrong reduction bucket
evidence_from_fix: `i` was Python-late-bound inside the closure, every hook fired with the same final value of `i`, routing earlier groups' gradients into the last group's bucket

relation_statement: The optimizer's per-param step counter must equal the number of real parameter updates performed, so it must still be zero immediately after engine construction.
observable_signal: Adam state['step'] value after initialization vs number of completed optimizer updates (expected 0)
validity_precondition: optimizer wrapped by sharded/low-precision engine that materializes state at construction
evidence_from_issue: optimizer.step() called once during initialization, increments Adam step counter before any real update
evidence_from_fix: eager step() during construction silently incremented state['step'] for every param, so bias-correction terms were off by one

relation_statement: The gradient accumulation buffer dtype must equal the model dtype whenever sharded-gradient reduction assumes matching dtypes.
observable_signal: dtype of the allocated grad-accumulation buffers vs model parameter dtype at engine init
validity_precondition: bf16 model with sharded optimizer (ZeRO) enabled and no explicit grad_accum_dtype configured
evidence_from_issue: BF16 model + ZeRO defaults silently force fp32 grad accum buffer despite ZeRO requiring matching dtype
evidence_from_fix: auto-selected fp32 for bf16 models; accumulation buffers in fp32 while reduction ran in bf16, so accumulated gradients were lost on the first cast back

relation_statement: Gradient reduction must fire exactly once per gradient-accumulation boundary, not once per micro-batch, under pipeline + sharded-optimizer training.
observable_signal: count of gradient all-reduce/reduce-scatter launches per optimizer step vs expected one per accumulation boundary
validity_precondition: pipeline parallel combined with ZeRO stage 2/3 and gradient_accumulation_steps > 1
evidence_from_issue: gradient accumulation boundary flag never propagated, ZeRO does early reduction every micro-step
evidence_from_fix: engine never told the optimizer whether it was at a real GAS boundary; reduction kicked off on every micro-batch, destroying accumulation correctness

relation_statement: The dataloader's reported length must equal the number of batches it actually yields (samples/batch_size with drop_last semantics), whenever downstream schedules consume it.
observable_signal: len(dataloader) vs the count of batches produced by one full iteration
validity_precondition: any consumer of len(dataloader) (lr schedule total steps, max_steps detection) with batch_size > 1
evidence_from_issue: DeepSpeedDataLoader.len reports sampler length, ignores batch_size and drop_last
evidence_from_fix: self.len was set to len(data_sampler), the sample count; callers received sample count instead of batch count, off by ~batch_size×

relation_statement: The gradient accumulation buffer must be allocated in the user-configured grad_accum_dtype rather than a hard-coded dtype.
observable_signal: dtype of the flat gradient-accumulation buffers vs configured grad_accum_dtype at init
validity_precondition: bf16 model without ZeRO, explicit grad_accum_dtype=bf16 requested in config
evidence_from_issue: BF16_Optimizer fp32 grad accumulator allocated as fp32 even when grad_acc_dtype is bf16
evidence_from_fix: ignored the requested grad_acc_dtype and always allocated fp32_groups_gradients_flat as fp32; step-time cast silently down-cast accumulated values

relation_statement: Any cached reference marking a gradient for reduction must be cleared or refreshed each iteration so that only current-iteration gradients enter the reduction, under non-contiguous gradient mode.
observable_signal: reduction consuming a gradient tensor produced in a previous iteration (stale pointer surviving across backward passes); divergence of reduced grads vs a fresh-recompute baseline
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 2 with contiguous_gradients=False and at least one param larger than reduce_bucket_size
evidence_from_issue: extra_large_param leaks reference when contiguous_gradients=False — silent stale-grad reduction in next step
evidence_from_fix: the assignment was a dead store but the reference outlived the iteration; the next backward saw the stale reference and reduced a previous-iteration gradient

relation_statement: The per-rank loss must be scaled by the expert-parallel group size before backward so that reduced expert gradients match the ep_size=1 equivalent.
observable_signal: reduced expert-gradient norm smaller by factor ep_size relative to the dense/ep=1 baseline; loss scale factor applied in backward vs ep_size
validity_precondition: AutoEP MoE layer under ZeRO stage 2 where each EP rank sees a token slice of one logical batch
evidence_from_issue: forgets to scale per-rank loss by EP-group size — expert gradients undercount by factor ep_size
evidence_from_fix: backward() does not multiply the loss by ep_size, so reduced expert gradients are scaled by 1/ep_size relative to the ep_size=1 baseline, biasing every step

relation_statement: Expert parameters must be re-sharded on resume using the true expert-data-parallel world size (dp/sp), so each rank restores exactly the slice it saved, under sequence parallelism.
observable_signal: per-rank expert parameter checksum before save vs after load; recorded dp_world_size field vs seq-adjusted dp world size
validity_precondition: MoE module present with sequence_parallel_size > 1 across a save/load cycle
evidence_from_issue: MoE checkpoint records dp_world_size instead of seq_dp_world_size — wrong replication factor on resume
evidence_from_fix: loader uses this value to re-shard expert tensors, producing the wrong split; each EP-rank loads weights for the wrong slice and starts from corrupted parameters

relation_statement: Reduced expert gradients must be averaged with the effective data-parallel world size as divisor, not the smaller expert-DP group size, when ep_size differs from dp_size.
observable_signal: reduced expert-gradient magnitude off by factor dp/edp relative to dense gradients; effective divisor applied in reduction vs dp world size
validity_precondition: MoE layers under ZeRO stage 1/2 with ep_size != dp_size
evidence_from_issue: expert gradients pre-divide by edp_world_size then skip the bucket-level divide — net divisor is dp/edp not dp
evidence_from_fix: the proper averaging factor should be dp_world_size, not edp_world_size; expert gradients are systematically off by a factor of (dp/edp)

relation_statement: Token dispatch locations must be recomputed from the current routing mask after any capacity update so that dispatch and combine address the same slots, under no-token-drop gating.
observable_signal: dispatch/combine round-trip mismatch: tokens scattered into expert slots inconsistent with the current mask/capacity (combine maps experts back to wrong tokens)
validity_precondition: MoE topk gating with drop_tokens=False and expert load varying across ranks (capacity raised via all_reduce MAX)
evidence_from_issue: drop_tokens=False does not recompute locations after capacity update — dispatch positions stale
evidence_from_fix: old locations from a stale earlier mask are used to scatter tokens into expert slots, so tokens go into the wrong dispatch positions

relation_statement: The cached secondary parameter partition must be invalidated or refreshed whenever the primary partition changes (weight load, checkpoint resume), before it feeds any allgather.
observable_signal: checksum mismatch between the allgathered full parameter and the master partition contents after a load event
validity_precondition: ZeRO-3 with hierarchical ZeRO++ secondary partitions, after GatheredParameters weight update or load_checkpoint
evidence_from_issue: ds_secondary_tensor stale after model load / checkpoint resume — dirty allgather poisons next forward
evidence_from_fix: secondary tensor was never refreshed after the master ds_tensor changed; next allgather constructs a corrupted parameter mixing new master weights with old secondary values

relation_statement: The quantized all-to-all reduction result must match the standard gradient reduction (within quantization error) for any actual GPUs-per-node count, i.e., buffer slicing must use the real local world size.
observable_signal: kernel divisor (gpu_per_node) vs actual local_world_size; reduced gradient mismatch against unquantized allreduce on non-16-GPU nodes
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with quantized gradients (qgZ) on nodes whose local world size != 16
evidence_from_issue: all_to_all_quant_reduce hard-codes gpu_per_node=16 — wrong intra-node split on every non-16-GPU node
evidence_from_fix: C++ side ignored the passed local_world_size; buffer slicing done with the wrong divisor attributes rows to the wrong intra-node rank, producing wrong reduced gradients

relation_statement: Repeated optimizer state-increment calls carrying the same logical step (one per parameter subgroup) must leave the bias-correction factors identical, so all subgroups apply the same Adam step.
observable_signal: betta1_t/betta2_t values observed across subgroup calls within one logical step; divergence of updated weights between subgroups given identical inputs
validity_precondition: CPU-offloaded Adam with multiple subgroup optimizer calls per logical step (ZeRO-3 sub_group_size > 0)
evidence_from_issue: IncrementStep non-idempotent across same-step subgroup updates — bias-correction drifts between subgroups
evidence_from_fix: first call takes the multiplicative branch, second falls through to the pow-recompute branch computing a different floating-point value, so subgroups see different betta1_t

relation_statement: The global gradient norm must aggregate the contributions of all tensor-parallel shards (counting replicated params once and sliced params from every rank) before clipping is applied.
observable_signal: reported total grad norm vs norm recomputed from gathered full gradients; systematic ratio ~1/sqrt(tp_size)
validity_precondition: fp16 fused optimizer with param groups containing genuinely TP-sliced parameters
evidence_from_issue: grad-norm reduces only TP-rank-0 gradients — TP grad_norm undercounted by sqrt(tp_size)
evidence_from_fix: treated the whole flat buffer as non-TP so only tp_rank=0 contributed; for TP-sliced parameters all per-rank slices should sum into the global norm, so clipping is weaker than configured

relation_statement: The cached per-parameter gradient norms must be refreshed whenever a partition's gradient is externally overwritten, so the clip factor reflects the gradients actually being clipped, under CPU offload.
observable_signal: scaled_global_grad_norm vs a norm recomputed directly from the current partition gradients after modification
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with CPU optimizer offload and gradients modified via safe_set_local_grad between backward and step
evidence_from_issue: set_local_grad does not refresh norm_for_param_grads — gradient clipping uses pre-clipping norm
evidence_from_fix: aggregate reflects pre-modification gradients while the clip factor based on this stale norm is applied to the modified grads — silent mis-clipping

relation_statement: Backward gradients under fp16 autocast must remain within fp16's representable range (via loss scaling) rather than systematically underflowing to zero, when no framework loss-scaler path is active.
observable_signal: fraction of exactly-zero gradient elements / collapse of gradient norm toward zero across steps
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 0 with torch.autocast(fp16) and no GradScaler instantiated
evidence_from_issue: trains without a GradScaler — fp16 gradients underflow to zero
evidence_from_fix: backward propagated unscaled fp16 grads; anything below ~6e-5 flushes to 0, optimizer applies near-zero updates and training stalls

relation_statement: The write of the next gradient bucket into the shared reduction buffer must be ordered after the in-flight allreduce finishes reading that buffer, under overlapped communication.
observable_signal: loss/gradient divergence between overlap_comm=True and overlap_comm=False runs on identical inputs; buffer overwritten while a reduction on it is still pending
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with overlap_comm=True and per-bucket allreduce slower than the next bucket's backward compute
evidence_from_issue: reduction stream not waited by current stream — ipg_buffer rewrite races allreduce when comm > compute
evidence_from_fix: current_stream did NOT wait_stream(reduction_stream); the next gradient gets written into the same buffer slot the allreduce is still reading, corrupting the reduce input

relation_statement: The averaged/reduced region of the gradient bucket buffer must cover exactly the valid gradient elements, excluding the uninitialized tail, whenever the bucket flushes before it is full.
observable_signal: reduced-buffer extent vs elements_in_ipg_bucket; contamination of end-of-bucket gradients relative to a full-precision recompute (nondeterministic garbage-dependent values)
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2, contiguous_gradients=True, bucket flushed with elements_in_ipg_bucket < reduce_bucket_size
evidence_from_issue: IPG buffer averaged over full allocated size — averages garbage from unused tail elements
evidence_from_fix: only elements_in_ipg_bucket are valid; stale tail floats get included in the all-reduce sum and divide, contaminating the averaged gradient slice near the end of the buffer

relation_statement: The sequence-parallel all-to-all reshape must preserve the (batch, sequence, head) identity of every token, so post-scatter activations correspond to the same logical tokens.
observable_signal: round-trip all_to_all followed by inverse all_to_all not reproducing the input layout; query[b,s,h] mapped to a different logical token than key/value
validity_precondition: distributed-attention sequence parallelism using the head-scatter (scatter_idx >= 2) all-to-all path
evidence_from_issue: single_all_to_all reshape collapses batch and seq dims — QKV permuted into wrong tokens
evidence_from_fix: reshape collapses batch and sequence and reorders elements such that query[b,s,h] no longer corresponds to the same logical token; attention computed on scrambled tokens

relation_statement: The manual scale_loss/backward path must apply the same expert-parallel output-gradient scale as engine.backward, so expert gradients are identical across the two API paths.
observable_signal: expert-gradient norm ratio between manual-backward and engine.backward runs on identical inputs (expected 1, observed 1/ep_size)
validity_precondition: AutoEP MoE present and user drives backward via engine.scale_loss(loss).backward() (e.g. HF Trainer integration)
evidence_from_issue: manual loss.backward path skips ep_size loss scaling — parity with engine.backward broken
evidence_from_fix: manual path forgot the AutoEP-specific multiplication by _autoep_output_grad_scale that engine.backward applies; expert gradients undercount by ep_size

relation_statement: Each data-parallel rank's offloaded optimizer state must be saved to and reloaded from a rank-exclusive location so every rank restores exactly its own shard.
observable_signal: per-rank optimizer state (exp_avg/exp_avg_sq) checksum before save vs after load; multiple ranks writing identical destination paths
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 3 with NVMe optimizer offload across a multi-rank save/load cycle
evidence_from_issue: NVMe optimizer offload writes all ranks' tensors to one shared dir — last writer wins, load gets wrong rank's state
evidence_from_fix: every rank's local NVMe state copied into the same directory, overwritten file-by-file; on load each rank initializes optimizer state from another rank's slice

relation_statement: The number of parameter elements stepped by the optimizer kernel must equal the parameter's total element count (numel), not just its first-dimension size.
observable_signal: fraction of parameter elements unchanged after an optimizer step despite nonzero gradients (all elements beyond the first row static)
validity_precondition: CPU Adam/Adagrad kernels applied to any parameter with ndim >= 2
evidence_from_issue: uses params.size(0) instead of numel() — only the first row of multi-dim params gets updated
evidence_from_fix: passed params_c.size(0) as the element count; for a (out, in) weight only `out` elements are stepped, the rest never receive an update

relation_statement: Init-time collective broadcasts of parameters must stay outside the autograd graph so that backward never differentiates through a synchronization op.
observable_signal: parameters carrying a grad_fn / broadcast node in their autograd history after engine init; gradient mismatch vs a run with non-differentiable broadcast
validity_precondition: engine init broadcast of model parameters with requires_grad=True (ZeRO 1/2 broadcast path)
evidence_from_issue: init broadcast tracked through autograd — backward through synchronization op silently corrupts gradients
evidence_from_fix: c10d::broadcast_ has no registered autograd kernel; autograd traverses the broadcast op and computes incorrect gradients silently

relation_statement: Gradient reduction must communicate in the configured communication_data_type (matching bf16 grads) rather than a hard-coded fp16 downcast.
observable_signal: dtype of tensors handed to the allreduce vs configured communication dtype; Inf/0 saturation of out-of-fp16-range gradient values
validity_precondition: bf16 model under ZeRO 1/2/3 with communication dtype expected to be bf16
evidence_from_issue: allreduce_bucket hard-codes communication_data_type=fp16 — bf16 grads silently downcast for reduction
evidence_from_fix: caller never passed self.communication_data_type, so all reductions converted bf16 grads to fp16; values outside fp16's range become Inf/0 and the rest lose precision

relation_statement: The optimizer's applied learning rate must equal the scheduler-defined value for the current step, including step 0 before the first scheduler.step().
observable_signal: optimizer.param_groups lr at the first optimizer step vs the scheduler's intended initial lr (warmup_min_lr)
validity_precondition: WarmupLR/LRRangeTest/OneCycle scheduler attached and optimizer constructed with a different (e.g. peak) lr
evidence_from_issue: schedulers do not initialize optimizer group lr at construction — first step uses original lr
evidence_from_fix: never wrote min_lr into param_groups; with 1e-4 peak lr and 0 warmup_min_lr the first update is ~10000x larger than intended

relation_statement: The scheduler's peak learning rate must equal the user-configured optimizer learning rate rather than a hard-coded default.
observable_signal: applied param-group lr trajectory vs the lr the user configured on the optimizer (observed pinned to 0.001)
validity_precondition: WarmupLR used without an explicit warmup_max_lr in the scheduler config
evidence_from_issue: WarmupLR ignores optimizer LR, always uses hardcoded 0.001
evidence_from_fix: warmup_max_lr defaults to 0.001 instead of inheriting from optimizer param_groups

relation_statement: Per-rank recorded padding must sum to the total alignment padding of the flattened group, so that padding-trimmed optimizer state covers exactly the true parameter elements on every rank.
observable_signal: sum of recorded per-rank padding vs (aligned size - group numel); trimmed optimizer-state length vs true parameter element count on padding-bearing ranks
validity_precondition: ZeRO stage 1/2 with DP world size large enough that alignment padding spans more than the last rank
evidence_from_issue: records padding only on last rank — middle ranks at large DP report padding=0 and contaminate optimizer state
evidence_from_fix: padding recorded only on partition_id == world_size-1; other padding ranks keep junk values treated as legitimate optimizer state on save
